newsitem.title: UK: TWA joins BA in French security fears.
newsitem.headline: TWA joins BA in French security fears.

text.p: U.S. airline Trans World Airlines joined British Airways Plc on Friday in expressing concern about security at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport due to last week's decision to allow Algeria's national airline to resume flights there.
But in Paris, the French civil aviation authority DGAC reaffirmed that the security measures in place at Charles de Gaulle were adequate.

"The high-security measures currently put in place by the national authorities are perfectly suited to the situation and are at least as good, to take one example, as those practiced by the British authorities at Heathrow," the DGAC said in a statement.

The DGAC also rejected, on a technicality, a plea by BA that its flights be transferred to Orly airport on the other side of Paris, informing the airline that it had addressed its demand to the wrong government agency.
BA has refused to use its check-in desks since Air Algerie became its neighbour last week, because of fears that it would be a target for Islamic guerrillas.
It wants to shift its flights to Orly unless Air Algerie is itself moved to a more secure area.

A spokesman for TWA in London told Reuters that under the new arrangements it was meant to share a satellite gate with Air Algerie. But the U.S. carrier has refused to park its aircraft alongside the Algerians.
Instead TWA has been busing passengers to and from its aircraft parked further out, airline spokesman Sam Nakamura said.

"We obviously take the issues of safety and security of our customers and staff very seriously. We are parking our aircraft at a remote location and taking passengers to and from the aircraft by coach," he said.
Nakamura said he remained hopeful that the dispute could be resolved.
"We continue to have discussions with the airport authorities and are optimistic about the resolution of the various issues," he said.
But BA said it was less confident.

"We have nothing against Air Algerie," said an airline spokesman. "But it appears that the French authorities are determined to try and force us either to accept the inadequate security arrangements or to inflict on us a grossly unsatisfactory level of customer service.
